event.name: 30 October 2020 Samos earthquake (eastern Aegean Sea, Greece–Türkiye)
event.tectonic_setting: North-dipping North Samos/Kaystrios normal fault in the active eastern Aegean extension zone, northern coast of Samos Island.
event.region: Samos Island–Kuşadası/İzmir, eastern Aegean Sea, Greece and Türkiye

reference.title: Characteristics of the 2020 Samos earthquake (Aegean Sea) using seismic data
reference.journal: Bulletin of Earthquake Engineering, 20, 7713–7735 (published online 2021; volume year 2022)

inversion.method: Non-negative least squares inversion of regional broadband seismic source-time functions (30 displacement components, 260–460 km). Assumed 1.8 s rise time, 2.2 km/s rupture speed; a 70×25 km plane discretized at 1×1 km, with rake variable ±45° around −98°. Figure 7a is the preferred coseismic solution.
inversion.green_function_model: Frequency-wavenumber Green functions using the 1-D Aegean velocity model of Novotný et al. (2001).
inversion.notes: VISUAL FIGURE DIGITIZATION — NOT AUTHORS ORIGINAL SLIP COEFFICIENTS. Kiratzi et al. (2022), Figure 7a on printed page 7726 (PDF page 14). Original finite-fault inversion plane: 70 km along strike × 25 km down dip, 1×1 km subfaults (1750 unknown original coefficients). Figure 7a displays only 0–20 km in down-dip coordinate, and approximately −40 to +40 km strike-relative plotting axis; digitized model consists of 70 columns (−35 to +35 km) × 20 visible down-dip rows (0–20 km). The 5 km unplotted downdip strip is OMITTED, not filled with zeros. Patch centers follow original 1-km sampling, image axis East on left, West on right. Colored raster quantized by an estimated continuous 0–3.5 m colorbar; resolution and interpolation produce larger uncertainties than 0.001 m output precision. Background white/offwhite values below ~0.08 m are represented as 0 for DISPLAY ONLY and may include low nonzero slip. Magenta rectangle marking the main rupture and the white hypocenter star were masked/interpolated locally; each patch carries a confidence class in the QA CSV. The authors inverted a variable rake ±45° around −98°; per-cell rake values are NOT retrievable from scalar slip Figure 7a. Patch rake −98° is a NOMINAL placeholder, not reconstructed variable rake. Top depth 0.5 km and planar-depth conversion from down-dip distance use the published principal fault geometry; patch geodetic coordinates were not directly provided and are left null. The source reports mean slip around 1 m within MAJOR SLIP PATCHES, not the entire plotted plane; the separate figure-digitized mean is 0.419 m over the 1400 visible sampled patches. The published preferred original fault plane differs from the displayed sampled 70×20 km window; do not infer missing lower rows.

provenance.compiled_by: Colorbar-calibrated per-original-1km-cell sampling of Kiratzi et al. (2022) Fig. 7a, excluding magenta polygon boundary and star. Visible-window model only (70×20 cells); full 70×25 source plane NOT reconstructed. Values are image-derived, not original inversion coefficients. Companion QA CSV documents cellwise overlay and confidence.
